cover.hook: Anthropic just filed to go public. The AI lab behind Claude is heading to Nasdaq — ticker ANT.
cover.sub: Plus OpenAI's biggest price cut in months, two FedNor wins for Northern Ontario, and a new US law restricting AI for kids.

reelSub: Five AI and funding moves NWO can't ignore this week.
storySub: What this week's AI and funding news means for a Northwestern Ontario business.

items.title: Anthropic files for Nasdaq IPO — ticker ANT
items.body: Anthropic filed its S-1 on October 26 with $16.3B in H1 2026 revenue. Going public changes the governance of the company behind Claude — NWO businesses on the Claude API now have a public company as a counterparty.
items.tease: Next: OpenAI cuts API costs in half.
items.reelLine: Anthropic just filed to go public — Nasdaq ticker ANT.

items.title: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra cuts API pricing in half
items.body: Released October 26. Replaces GPT-5.6 Terra at half the per-token cost. Available in the API, ChatGPT Work, and Codex same day. If you're on the old model, a swap could cut your API spend immediately.
items.tease: Next: $4.5M for Northern Ontario's underground mining-tech lab.
items.reelLine: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra at half the price of its predecessor.

items.title: FedNor expands NORCAT's underground innovation centre
items.body: Ottawa committed $4.5M on October 30 to expand NORCAT's Sudbury underground centre — the primary Northern Ontario lab for testing autonomous systems and robotics in mining conditions. Capacity up 50%.
items.tease: Next: $3.8M for NWO agri-food businesses in Toronto.
items.reelLine: FedNor put $4.5M into NORCAT's underground mining-tech centre.

items.title: FedNor sends 40+ NWO agri-food businesses to the Royal Winter Fair
items.body: Ottawa put $3,817,640 through three FedNor programs on October 29 to fund the Northern Ontario Agri-Food Pavilion at Canada's largest indoor agricultural show — November 6-15 in Toronto.
items.tease: Next: the first US law banning unsafe AI features for kids.
items.reelLine: FedNor backed 40+ NWO agri-food businesses at the Royal Agricultural Winter Fair.

items.title: New York bans unsafe AI chatbot features for users under 18
items.body: Governor Hochul signed the first US state AI-for-minors law on October 28. Banned: companion personas, self-harm nudges, AI pretending to be human. Up to $25K per violation. Not Ontario law today — but the model Canadian legislators are watching.
items.reelLine: New York signed the first US law restricting unsafe AI features for minors.

summary.title: The AI industry's governance is changing — at every level
summary.body: Anthropic files to go public, OpenAI cuts prices, New York regulates AI for kids, and FedNor invests in Northern Ontario's mining-tech and agri-food infrastructure — the week AI oversight got louder at the corporate, legislative, and regional level simultaneously.
